paras: The death of an unidentified Black man near Reagan, Texas, came to light around Christmas 1881, when his body was found on a railroad track near the town after two trains had reportedly passed over it. The Waco Daily Examiner, the only paper found to report it, suggested that unknown persons had killed and robbed him and left his body on the track to hide the crime.

The Examiner described the finding as the first of several violent incidents during "Last Saturday and Sunday" in "Waco and surroundings," that is, December 24 and 25, 1881, though it did not give the day the body was found. The paper said it could not learn the man's name and had been "informed that two trains passed over him." According to further reports it repeated, he had been seen carrying a bundle of clothes and was known to have money, and both were missing when the body was found. From this the paper concluded that "it is thought" he was killed by "some unknown parties" and his remains placed on the track "as a blind to cover their villainy."
No report of an inquest, an identification of the man, or any arrest appears in the coverage.

The death appeared only as the opening paragraph of a local roundup in the Examiner of December 27, 1881, headlined "Christmas Diversions. Two Negroes Killed and a Nymph Badly Bombarded." The item set the death beside a pistol assault between two women of the "demi-monde" and the shooting of Bob Graves by Nath. Williams below Waco, presenting all three as holiday "acts of violence" among "the colored people and demimonde." The paper offered its theory of murder as hearsay, made no further comment on the dead man, and closed by remarking that such scenes "sadly mar" the Christmas festivities.
No other white paper and no Black paper in the collections searched carried the story.

accounts.label: Waco Daily Examiner (local hearsay)
accounts.gist: The body of a nameless Black man was found on the track near Reagan after two trains passed over it; because his bundle and money were gone, it was 'thought' he had been killed by unknown parties and placed on the track to hide the crime.

framing.detail: Headlined 'CHRISTMAS DIVERSIONS. Two Negroes Killed and a Nymph Badly Bombarded.', the item treats the death as one of several holiday 'acts of violence' among 'the colored people and demimonde', with no comment on the victim.

record_check.dossier: A1 does not date the finding; it falls among events of 'last Saturday and Sunday' (Dec. 24-25), so ~1881-12-24/25 is an approximation.
No county is given; A1 places Reagan only in 'Waco and surroundings'. A later Marlin dispatch reporting news from Reagan (A3) suggests the town may lie in the Marlin area, so the county is uncertain.
other: an unexplained death that the paper suspected was a robbery-murder by unknown persons; no mob or lynching is described.

sources.note: Only report: local roundup 'Christmas Diversions'; body of an unnamed negro found on the railroad track near Reagan, money and bundle missing, paper thinks he was killed and placed on the track 'as a blind'.

set_aside: Texas telegraphic column (Dallas, Hillsboro, San Antonio, Houston); 'Reagan' here is Hon. John H. Reagan; nothing on this death.
A Marlin dispatch reports a fire at Reagan; unrelated, but shows Reagan news reaching Waco via Marlin, which bears on the county.

acts.note: Killing is the paper's surmise ('it is thought'); body found on track after two trains reportedly passed over it.

actors.who: 'some unknown parties' suspected by the paper

override.why: body found on a railroad track; robbery guessed, accident possible: not a lynching
